body.statement: What is the exact minimax expected-length frontier for replacement-private, uniformly honest intervals for \(\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\) over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\)? In particular, can the positive-density confidence-modulus handle reduce the higher-order release sensitivity while retaining the uniform bias guarantee, or can it certify that an additional nuisance-driven privacy term is unavoidable?
body.justification: The gap between the ordinary full-class lower bound and the constructive higher-order upper phase is the genuine unresolved mathematical content.
body.gap: Neither KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 nor the located private CATE and private confidence-interval papers characterize this privacy-constrained confidence modulus.
body.consumer: A resolution determines whether private heterogeneous-treatment-effect studies pay only the ordinary local-regression privacy price or an irreducible higher-order nuisance price.
